pages.title: About
pages.content:
ABOUT

A frame for
a conversation.

Waku Exhibits has planned and built exhibition stands from Unit 4, Harbour Works, in Lindhaven since 2014. “Waku” means frame: the stand is there to hold a conversation, not to shout over it.

THE WORKSHOP · UNIT 4, HARBOUR WORKS

We stand it up here first

Before a stand travels to a hall, we build it once in our workshop. Samuel Okoye, our workshop foreman, checks every joint and every panel edge, and the team walks the stand with the drawing in hand.

Anything that does not fit is fixed on our floor, not in the hall at six in the morning. It is the least glamorous part of the job and the one clients mention most.

#Workshop #Prebuild #Timber

THE PEOPLE · EIGHT OF US

Planners, makers, builders

Ines Marlow founded the studio in 2014 after years of planning stands for other builders. She still does most of the hall walks, with Lena Vasquez handling hall rules and logistics, and Mei Lin Hart booking every planning hour at the client desk.

Tomas Reyes, Aiko Brandt, Priya Nair, Jonas Feld and Samuel Okoye make and fit the stand. We are small on purpose: the person who plans your stand is in the hall when it goes up.

#Planning #Making #Onsite

Who you will meet

Eight people, each with a name on the quote. A written quote comes from the planner who walked your hall, not from a sales desk.

  • Ines Marlow · Founder and lead planner. Runs most planning hours on the hall floor.
  • Tomas Reyes · Structural lead. Aluminium and timber systems, load paths and fixings.
  • Aiko Brandt · Graphics and print production. Colour proofs on the real board.
  • Samuel Okoye · Workshop foreman. Owns the pre-build and the crates.
  • Lena Vasquez · Project manager. Logistics, hall rules and paperwork.
  • Priya Nair · Lighting and power. Plans every socket and spotlight before the build.
  • Jonas Feld · On-site build supervisor. Leads the crew in the hall.
  • Mei Lin Hart · Client desk. Books your planning hour and answers first.

How we work

We plan on the floor, quote in writing and build twice: once in the workshop, once in the hall. A written quote follows within five working days of the planning hour, and the €180 for that hour is credited to the build if you go ahead. We do not promise outcomes at a show; we promise a stand that goes up as drawn.

• Request a stand quote

pages.title: Halls
pages.content:
HALLS

Halls a quote
suits.

Trade fair halls, conference foyers, pop-up and retail atriums, and touring stands. Each has its own rules, build windows and floor loads; we read them before we draw.

HALL 01 · 18–120 m²

Trade fair halls

Row, corner and island stands from 18 to 120 m² in Messe-style halls. We read the organiser’s technical guidelines first: maximum height, hanging points, floor loads and the build and dismantle windows.

Ines walks the allotted plot with tape before anything is drawn, so the quote reflects the real columns, hatches and power points.

#Messe #Island #Corner

HALL 02 · 9–24 m²

Conference foyers

Sponsor stands of 9 to 24 m² that stay under the venue’s height limit, stand on carpet without drilling and go up quietly while delegates are still arriving.

We plan around fire routes, glass walls and the catering flow, and keep the build to the early-morning window the venue allows.

#Foyer #Sponsor #LowHeight

HALL 03 · 4–30 m²

Pop-up & retail atriums

Compact stands of 4 to 30 m² built under mall management rules. Panels arrive pre-finished and the build runs between 22:00 and 06:00 with silent battery tools.

We cover floors, protect escalator edges and leave the atrium clean for opening.

#Atrium #NightBuild #Pop-up

HALL 04 · 3–8 shows a year

Touring stands

Modular aluminium and timber kits designed to be rebuilt at 3 to 8 shows a year. Every panel is numbered, every crate is packed in build order, and the kit is stored with us between shows.

The layout changes with each hall; the kit and the crates do not.

#Touring #Modular #Reuse

Read the hall rules before we draw the first line.

pages.title: Stand types
pages.content:
STAND TYPES

Four stand types,
one process.

A 9 m² shell-scheme upgrade from €2,400, an 18 m² row stand from €7,800, a 36 m² corner stand from €14,500 and a 72 m² island stand from €29,000 (EUR, excl. VAT).

STAND 01 · 9 m² · FROM €2,400

Shell-scheme upgrade

The organiser’s standard shell, lifted with timber panels, a proper counter and lighting. The quickest way to look intentional in a hall that gives you four white walls.

Built from kit parts that return to our workshop and are reused.

#Shell #Upgrade #Kit

STAND 02 · 18 m² · FROM €7,800

Custom row stand

One open side to the aisle. We design the stand around a single clear idea, such as a demo table, a meeting corner or a product wall, and light it so it reads from the far end of the hall.

Includes pre-build in the workshop and a graphics proof on the real board.

#Row #Custom #Lighting

STAND 03 · 36 m² · FROM €14,500

Corner stand

Two open sides and more room to talk. The corner suits a meeting zone, a storage room and a counter, and it is where the hall’s columns and hatches matter most.

See “The pillar we built around” in the stories for one we planned on the floor.

#Corner #Meeting #Storage

STAND 04 · 72 m² · FROM €29,000

Island stand

Open on all four sides under the hall’s trusses. Rigging points, sightlines from every aisle and the build crew’s lift access are planned before the drawing starts.

The largest stand we build, and the one where the planning hour matters most.

#Island #Rigging #Sightlines

pages.title: Planning hour
pages.content:
PLANNING HOUR

Sixty minutes
on the hall floor.

15 minutes on the hall plan and rules, 20 minutes walking the footprint with tape, 15 minutes on materials and reuse, 10 minutes on budget and dates. A written quote follows within 5 working days.

Five steps, in order

1 Request. Fill in the short form; it takes about two minutes. Mei Lin replies within one working day to book a time.

2 Planning hour. Sixty minutes with Ines or one of the planners, on the hall floor or by video with the hall plan open. €180, credited to the build.

3 Written quote. Within five working days of the hour, itemised and in EUR, with the drawing we made together.

4 Workshop pre-build. If you go ahead, we stand the stand up in our workshop first and fix what does not fit.

5 Hall build and dismantle. Our crew builds to the hall’s windows and takes the stand down again after the show.

THE SIXTY MINUTES

Where the hour goes

Four parts, always in this order, so the quote that follows reflects the hall and not a guess. You leave with a taped footprint and a list of what to decide next.

15 min

Hall plan & rules

20 min

Walking the footprint with tape

15 min

Materials & reuse

10 min

Budget & dates

ON THE FLOOR · 20 MIN OF THE HOUR

We tape it out together

The footprint goes down in orange tape and you walk it: where the counter sits, where people stop, where the aisle bends. Most changes are made here, in minutes, at no cost.

#Footprint #Tape #Hall

BY VIDEO · WITH THE HALL PLAN

If you cannot be in the hall

Send us the organiser’s hall plan and technical guidelines and we plan the hour by video. We mark the footprint on the plan together and agree what to check on site.

The quote is the same; only the tape stays in the workshop.

#Video #Hallplan #Remote

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY

A plan, a list and a date

A marked-up footprint, a short list of decisions still open and the date your written quote arrives. If you do not go ahead, you keep all of it.

#Plan #Materials #Quote

What to bring

  • The organiser’s hall plan with your plot marked, or the stand number.
  • The technical guidelines and any hall rules for the show.
  • Brand files: logo, colours and any graphics already printed.
  • The show dates, the build window and a rough budget range.

pages.title: Prices
pages.content:
PRICES

Prices,
itemised.

The planning hour is €180 and is credited to the build if you go ahead. All prices are in EUR excluding VAT.

Notes

  • All prices are “from” prices in EUR and exclude VAT.
  • A deposit of 30% confirms the build; the balance follows the show.
  • The €180 planning hour is credited to the build if you go ahead.
  • Quotes are valid for 30 days and arrive within 5 working days of the planning hour.
  • Touring kits and storage are priced per show and per month; stored kits can be collected at any time.

Questions we hear

What does the planning hour cost?

€180, excluding VAT. If you go ahead with a build, the full amount is credited against it.

Is a “from” price a fixed price?

No. It is the starting point for a stand of that size. The written quote after the planning hour is itemised and based on your hall, your materials and your dates.

When do I pay?

A deposit of 30% confirms the build. The balance is invoiced after the show. Storage is billed monthly.

Can I reuse a stand at another show?

Yes. That is what the touring kit is for: from €1,900 per show to rebuild it, plus storage at €95 a month between shows.

How long is a quote valid?

30 days from the date on it. If your show moves, tell us and we will re-check the dates.

Do you quote in other currencies?

No. Every price is in EUR and we do not convert, so the figure on the quote is the figure on the invoice.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
PRIVACY

Privacy.

We use the details you send us only to answer your request and prepare your quote. We do not sell them and we keep them for as long as the quote is open.

What we collect

When you request a quote we receive your name, company, email address, the show and hall, the stand size, dates and anything you write in the message. When you join the early-access list we receive your email address.

How we use it

Mei Lin Hart and the planner who walks your hall use these details to book the planning hour and to write your quote. If you join the early-access list, we use your address to send a few emails a year about hall-season dates and the touring-kit waitlist.

How long we keep it

Request details are kept while the quote is open and for a reasonable time after, so we can answer questions about it. Early-access addresses stay until you unsubscribe.

Who sees it

Our own team. We do not sell your details or pass them to advertisers. Where a hall organiser needs a contractor list for an approved build, we share only what the organiser asks for.

Your choices

Write to quotes@waku-exhibits.example to see, correct or delete what we hold, or to leave the early-access list. We answer within five working days.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
TERMS

Terms.

Quotes are valid for 30 days. A deposit of 30% confirms the build. Prices are in EUR excluding VAT.

Quotes

A written quote follows within 5 working days after the planning hour and is valid for 30 days from its date. “From” prices on this site are starting points; the quote is the price.

Planning hour

The planning hour is €180 excluding VAT. It is credited to the build if you go ahead with Waku Exhibits within the 30 days of the quote.

Deposit and payment

A deposit of 30% confirms the build and the dates. The balance is invoiced after the show. Storage between shows is billed monthly at €95 a month.

Changes and cancellation

Changes to the drawing after the quote is accepted are priced separately. If you cancel, the deposit covers the work already done; we will show you what that was.

Liability

We build to the drawing and to the hall’s published rules. We do not promise results at a show. Our liability for a build is limited to the price of that build, except where the law says otherwise.

posts.title: The pillar we built around
posts.excerpt: A 36 m² corner stand where a hall column became the meeting table.
posts.content:
The hall column sat exactly where the client wanted the meeting zone of a 36 m² corner stand. It was a plain concrete column, a little over half a metre across, and it was holding up the hall’s mezzanine. Moving it was not an option, and neither was pretending it was not there.

The planning hour

Ines Marlow met the client on the hall floor on a Tuesday morning. We had the organiser’s plan, the technical guidelines and a roll of orange tape. In the first twenty minutes of the hour we walked the plot, and the column simply kept getting in the way of every layout the client had imagined: a round table, a sofa, a screen on the back wall.

So we stopped drawing and asked a different question: what could the column do? We taped the footprint around it, then taped a table that wrapped it on two sides. Standing there, the client could see that the column would sit in the middle of a conversation rather than at the edge of one.

What we built

Tomas Reyes designed a timber table that wraps the column on two sides, with a slim shelf at standing height on the third. The table is solid birch ply on an aluminium frame, scribed to the column so there is no gap to collect coffee cups. The column carries a screen on a bracket that clamps without drilling, which is what the hall’s rules required.

The stand’s one open corner now faces the aisle, and the table seats six. A short counter sits against the back wall for brochures and charging. Priya Nair put the lighting in the column’s shadow, so the meeting zone is the best-lit part of the stand and the column itself becomes a quiet backdrop.

In the workshop first

We built the whole stand once in our workshop at Harbour Works, with a plywood and tape mock-up of the column standing where the real one would be. Samuel Okoye’s crew found two things we would otherwise have found in the hall: the table needed a 12 mm relief at the base for the hall’s uneven floor, and one of the shelf brackets fouled the screen cable.

In the hall

The build window was a single day. Jonas Feld’s crew carried the numbered panels in, fitted the frame in the morning and the timber in the afternoon, and Aiko Brandt’s graphics went on last. The stand opened to visitors the next morning. The client later told us the column had become the first thing people leaned on when they arrived.

What we would repeat

Not the table itself: it was drawn for that column and that client. What we would repeat is the order of the work. A hall obstacle is only a problem until it has been walked, taped and talked about. The planning hour is where that happens, and the workshop build is where we prove it.

If you have a column, a hatch or a low beam in your plot, mention it when you request a quote. It is usually the most interesting part of the brief.

posts.title: Three shows, one kit
posts.excerpt: A touring stand for a valve maker, reused in three halls.
posts.content:
A valve maker needed one stand for three shows in a season. We designed an aluminium and timber kit and built it up once in the workshop.

In each hall we changed the layout, not the panels: a row stand, a corner stand, then a narrower island. The crates travelled the same way each time.

posts.title: A night build in the atrium
posts.excerpt: A 12 m² pop-up assembled between 22:00 and 06:00.
posts.content:
The retail centre allowed building only after closing. We pre-finished every panel in the workshop and arrived at 22:00 with silent cordless tools.

By 06:00 the 12 m² pop-up was standing, lit and cleaned, and the atrium opened on time.
